title: Still learning, and her big band since 1986
summary: She attends master classes, wants to learn arranging, and describes her big band, founded 1986, in which she plays baritone, with arrangements by Charlie Camilleri.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Are you still a learner? Speaking of learning?

I try to attend as many — whenever I hear of a master class I try to go. I recently attended one on clarinet. I can’t remember the names of the two players, they were both great and it was like half and half — half the day and half the day — with these two amazing clarinetists teaching different students. And you know, I mean yeah, I try to learn, watch videos, go to master classes, whatever I have time for, go listen to players and I think that we always keep learning yeah, definitely. And plus I mean I’ve never learned to arrange and that’s something I still want to do. You know I have a big band. I guess you know that, or maybe you don’t. But it’s not my arrangements. Only one is something I arranged. But we’ve had the band since 1986 and I’m the bari player of course. And we get grants to perform and we have writers that write for us, and the biggest part of our library is by Charlie Camilleri, who is now gone, passed away, but he was — he wrote I would say over 40 or 50 arrangements for us.
